title: Focus and Flow Pack
description: For parents supporting kids 6–9 who find focus and transitions challenging. These routines blend structure and play to build executive function skills.

routines.title: Three-Step Start Chart
routines.description: Create a visual start routine for tasks like homework or chores.
routines.parentGoal: Provide predictable structure to lower task resistance.
routines.childOutcome: Improved initiation and confidence starting tasks.
steps: Draw three simple icons: timer, task, sticker.
Point to each as you go: 'Timer on, do one piece, sticker done.'
Celebrate with a high-five or smile.

routines.title: Movement Sandwich
routines.description: Use short bursts of movement before and after focus time.
routines.parentGoal: Support attention through rhythmic movement and breaks.
steps: Say, 'We’ll do 3 minutes of movement, then 10 minutes of focus, then 2 minutes of movement.'
Pick movements: jump rope, dance, crawl races.
End with praise for effort, not outcome.

routines.title: Body Fuel Break
routines.description: Offer a water and protein snack before focus time.
routines.parentGoal: Ensure physiological needs are met to support attention.
steps: Offer choices: 'Water or milk? Cheese stick or nuts?'
Avoid sugar-heavy snacks before focus time.
Share a quick 'cheers' moment before starting.

routines.title: See the Time
routines.description: Use a visual or analog timer for short focus bursts.
routines.parentGoal: Make time tangible to support executive function.
steps: Set timer for 10 minutes and show the child the countdown.
Say, 'Let’s see how far we get before it dings.'
Celebrate with a small win when time’s up.

routines.title: Bedtime Rock & Read
routines.description: End the day with gentle rocking or swaying while reading together.
routines.parentGoal: Ease the transition to sleep and model calm routines.
routines.childOutcome: Improved sleep onset and emotional security.
steps: Dim the lights and choose a short, calm story.
Hold or sway gently while reading.
